parcel_record.note: Per-record-licensed county parcel data. A request whose field selection includes ANY of these bills the group price ONCE per location — not once per field, because it is one purchased record — on top of fetch_credits_per_field for the other fields in the same request.

billing.note: Credits for one location = fetch_credits_per_field x the non-group fields requested, plus each metered group's price once if any of its fields is requested. A batch multiplies that by the number of locations. Full price list: GET /v1/meta/plans.

fields.description: Ground elevation above the NAVD88 vertical datum at the queried point. Sourced from the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second seamless DEM (~10m), with the USGS EPQS dynamic service as a coverage fallback.
fields.interpretation_hints: Below 10m within 5km of MARINE coast → storm-surge exposure relevant, but coast_distance_m does NOT establish that the nearby shoreline is marine — it also measures tidal rivers and estuaries, so it reads a few metres at points tens of km inland (Philadelphia ~13 m, the Anacostia in DC ~215 m). Confirm the shoreline is genuinely marine before drawing the surge conclusion from this pair. Above 3000m → alpine permitting, snow loads. Combine with coast_distance_m and within_floodplain_polygon for flood-zone reasoning.
fields.name: elevation

fields.description: Surface slope in degrees, computed from the USGS 3DEP DEM at the queried point. 0 = flat; 90 = vertical.
fields.interpretation_hints: Slope >15° materially raises wildfire spread risk on forested land. Slope >25° complicates conventional construction. Combine with lcms_class and dist_to_wui_m for wildfire underwriting.
fields.name: slope_degrees

fields.description: Slope aspect (compass bearing the slope faces) in degrees, 0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W.
fields.name: aspect_degrees

fields.description: Slope aspect as a cardinal direction (N, NE, E, ..., NW) — the compass direction the slope faces.
fields.name: aspect_cardinal

fields.description: Geodesic distance from the queried point to the nearest point on the nearest NOAA CUSP shoreline feature (measured to the SEGMENT, not to a vertex). CUSP charts every tidal shoreline it maps — open coast, bays and estuaries, the full tidal reach of rivers, and harbour structures such as bulkheads, wharves and breakwaters — so this is distance to NOAA-mapped SHORELINE, not distance to open ocean. A tidal-river waterfront therefore reads metres while the open sea is a hundred kilometres away: Philadelphia reads ~13 m against ~89 km of open sea, and the Anacostia in DC reads a few hundred metres against ~163 km. The value is only large where no CUSP feature is near at all (interior states). A small value therefore does NOT establish marine exposure on its own, and cannot carry a storm-surge inference until the matched shoreline is independently confirmed to be marine — stated here as well as in the interpretation hints, because the public field-catalog table renders descriptions only. Channelized inland water (Man-made.Canal*, Man-made.Lock) is excluded. Always populated.
fields.interpretation_hints: A small value means the nearest NOAA-CHARTED shoreline is close — which may be open coast, a bay, an estuary, a tidal-river bank or a harbour bulkhead — and NOT that open ocean is close; this field alone cannot distinguish them. The storm-surge inference (small distance + low elevation) is therefore CONDITIONAL on the matched shoreline being marine, and this field does not establish that, so do NOT conclude surge exposure from a small value on an inland tidal waterway — at waterfront points, Philadelphia reads 13 m, Sacramento 91 m and the Hudson at Poughkeepsie 134 m, and all three are 89-125 km from open sea. Coastal-zone permitting at <5km is the safer read, since jurisdiction generally follows tidal reach rather than the open shore. Calibration — at genuinely coastal points CUSP agrees with the OSM coastline to within ~38 m, so the value is excellent AT the shoreline, and every figure quoted here is a WATERFRONT reading: the same town measured a few hundred metres inland reads a few hundred metres, so a value is only comparable against another value taken at the shore. The Great Lakes are only PATCHILY covered, so two lakefront points on the same lake can read ~1 m (Sackets Harbor) and ~108 km (Rochester, at Charlotte on the lake), and the Chicago Loop resolves 1,047 km away to an inland reservoir in Georgia charted as Natural.Great Lake Or Lake Or Pond — not to any marine shoreline and not to Lake Michigan — which makes a Great Lakes lakefront value meaningless. Pair with elevation for flood reasoning and with aspect for hurricane orientation only once marine exposure is independently established. This field cannot answer how far the open ocean is; if that is the question, say so rather than substituting this value.
fields.name: coast_distance_m

fields.description: USDA SSURGO soil drainage class at the queried point (e.g. 'Well drained', 'Poorly drained', 'Excessively drained').
fields.interpretation_hints: Natural drainage class of the dominant gNATSGO component — a screen for wetness/ponding and foundation/earthwork suitability, not a site-specific drainage survey. Served from the gNATSGO 30 m dominant-component grid, which mixes detailed SSURGO (1:12-24k) with coarse STATSGO2 (1:250k) gap-fill where SSURGO is unmapped; a STATSGO2-sourced value is confidence-capped at MEDIUM and note-flagged.
fields.name: soil_drainage_class

fields.description: USDA SSURGO soil map-unit name at the queried point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Human-readable name of the gNATSGO map unit at the point (e.g. 'Branyon clay, 0 to 1 percent slopes', or 'Urban land'). Context for the other soil fields, not a determination on its own. Served from the gNATSGO 30 m grid, which mixes detailed SSURGO (1:12-24k) with coarse STATSGO2 (1:250k) gap-fill; a STATSGO2-sourced value is confidence-capped at MEDIUM.
fields.name: soil_map_unit_name

fields.description: Depth to bedrock in centimeters from USDA STATSGO. Censored at the dataset's measurement ceiling for deep-bedrock locations.
fields.name: bedrock_depth_cm

fields.description: True if the queried point intersects a USGS NHDPlus HR NHDArea hydrographic polygon, such as a stream/river area, canal/ditch, inundation area, wash, levee, or other areal hydrographic landmark.
fields.interpretation_hints: This is a source-specific USGS hydrography signal. It is not a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area or regulatory flood-risk determination; use within_floodplain_polygon for FEMA NFHL.
fields.name: intersects_nhd_area

fields.description: Name of the nearest USGS NHDPlus stream / river flowline.
fields.name: nearest_flowline_name
fields.null_meaning: Nearest NHDPlus flowline is unnamed or no flowline was found.

fields.description: Name of the nearest USGS NHDPlus waterbody (lake, reservoir, pond).
fields.name: nearest_waterbody_name
fields.null_meaning: Nearest NHDPlus waterbody is unnamed or no waterbody was found.

fields.description: Name of the USGS HUC-12 watershed containing the queried point.
fields.name: huc_12_name
fields.null_meaning: The point does not intersect any WBD HUC-12 subwatershed polygon (open ocean, or outside the dataset's U.S.+territories coverage), or the local WBD index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: True if the queried point falls inside a FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer Special Flood Hazard Area polygon.
fields.interpretation_hints: True → FEMA SFHA_TF is true or the flood-zone attributes classify as a Special Flood Hazard Area. False → FEMA returned a non-SFHA zone such as Zone X, or confirmed NFHL coverage with no intersecting Flood Hazard Zones polygon.
fields.name: within_floodplain_polygon

fields.description: True if the queried point falls inside a USFWS National Wetlands Inventory polygon (a biological wetland definition).
fields.interpretation_hints: NWI is NOT a regulatory or jurisdictional determination. A hit is a flag to investigate, not a §404 finding. Do NOT state 'USACE-jurisdictional' or 'permit required' from NWI alone — jurisdiction requires a USACE delineation / Approved Jurisdictional Determination; post-Sackett (2023), mapped wetlands lacking a continuous surface connection to a permanent water may not be federally regulated, while some states regulate more broadly. 'False' does NOT mean 'no wetland' where NWI is unmapped (e.g. Alaska) or imagery is stale — corroborate with soil_drainage_class (hydric soils) and nearest_flowline_name.
fields.name: intersects_wetland

fields.description: Decoded Cowardin classification of the wetland at (or nearest to) the point, in plain English (e.g. 'Palustrine Emergent Persistent Temporarily Flooded'). Falls back to the coarse NWI WETLAND_TYPE 8-bucket (e.g. 'Freshwater Forested/Shrub Wetland') when a code cannot be decoded.
fields.interpretation_hints: The biological class of the wetland. Palustrine Forested/Emergent near a stream is the common riparian finding. Read with wetland_subtype (the raw Cowardin code) for the exact federal code. Same caveat as intersects_wetland — type does NOT establish §404 status; NWI is a biological, not a regulatory/jurisdictional, classification.
fields.name: wetland_type
fields.null_meaning: No NWI wetland polygon within the 500 m search.

fields.description: Raw Cowardin classification code from NWI ATTRIBUTE (e.g. 'PFO1A' = Palustrine / Forested / Broad-Leaved Deciduous / Temporarily Flooded).
fields.interpretation_hints: The precise federal classification for expert users. First letter = System (P palustrine, R riverine, L lacustrine, E estuarine, M marine). Pair with wetland_type (plain-English). Not a jurisdiction code.
fields.name: wetland_subtype
fields.null_meaning: No NWI wetland polygon within the 500 m search.

fields.description: Total acreage of the NWI wetland polygon at (or nearest to) the point — NOT the share of any parcel.
fields.interpretation_hints: This is the whole mapped polygon's size, which may extend far beyond a given site. Do NOT present it as 'wetland on this parcel'. On-site coverage requires intersecting the parcel boundary (a separate capability). Use for 'how large is the wetland feature here', not 'how much of my land is wetland'.
fields.name: wetland_acres
fields.null_meaning: No NWI wetland polygon within the 500 m search.

fields.description: Geodesic meters to the nearest NWI wetland within a 500 m search; 0 if the point is on a wetland; null if none within 500 m.
fields.interpretation_hints: 0 = on a wetland; a small value = adjacent (adjacency matters for the post-Sackett continuous-surface-connection test); null = none within 500 m (NOT 'no wetland anywhere' — the search is capped at 500 m). Combine with nearest_flowline_name to reason about wetland-to-stream connection.
fields.name: nearest_wetland_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No NWI wetland polygon within the 500 m search radius.

fields.description: Count of NWI wetland polygons within 100 m of the point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Local wetland density (immediate buildable-area impact). 0 within 100 m plus intersects_wetland False = likely clear immediate footprint, but still verify by delineation.
fields.name: wetlands_within_100m_count

fields.description: Count of NWI wetland polygons within 500 m of the point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Wider wetland context / cumulative-impact and adjacency signal. Pair with nearest_wetland_distance_m.
fields.name: wetlands_within_500m_count

fields.description: JRC Global Surface Water permanence percentage at the queried 30m cell (0 = never surface water, 100 = permanent open water).
fields.interpretation_hints: 100 → point is on permanent open water. 10-90 → seasonal / intermittent water; combine with wetlands. 0 → no surface water in the cell.
fields.name: surface_water_permanence_pct

fields.description: USFS Land Change Monitoring System dominant land-cover class at the queried point, served from a bootstrapped ~120m block-mode CONUS grid (annual LCMS product). Life-form taxonomy — classes include Trees, Shrubs, Grass/Forb/Herb, cover mixes, Barren or Impervious, Water, Snow or Ice (no dedicated crop class). CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: 'Trees' + slope_degrees>15 + low NDVI change → wildfire-prone forested landscape. 'Barren or Impervious' in urban areas usually means paved/built — confirm with primary_building. For crop specificity drill into cdl_class. 'Water' → confirm with surface_water_permanence_pct.
fields.name: lcms_class
fields.null_meaning: Outside the served LCMS CONUS grid footprint (AK/HI/PRUSVI/ocean) or on a non-processing/nodata cell, or the raster is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: USFS LCMS land-use class (Agriculture / Developed / Forest / Other / Rangeland or Pasture / Non-Processing Area Mask), served from a bootstrapped ~120m block-mode CONUS grid. CONUS only.
fields.name: land_use_class
fields.null_meaning: Outside the served LCMS CONUS grid footprint (AK/HI/PRUSVI/ocean) or on a non-processing/nodata cell, or the raster is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Tree canopy cover percentage (0-100) at the point, sampled from the USFS/NLCD Tree Canopy Cover product served as a bootstrapped ~120m CONUS grid. CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: >60% canopy → dense forest; major wildfire fuel + cooling/shade benefit. <10% canopy → effectively non-forested for fire-risk purposes. CONUS only (served from a ~120m block-mean canopy % grid).
fields.name: tree_canopy_pct
fields.null_meaning: Outside the served NLCD TCC CONUS grid footprint (AK/HI/PRUSVI/ocean) or on a nodata/non-processing cell, or the raster is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Most recent Sentinel-2 NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) at the queried cell, range -1 to +1. Higher = greener / more photosynthetic activity.
fields.name: ndvi_current

fields.description: 5-year change in NDVI at the queried cell. Negative values indicate vegetation loss; positive indicate growth or recovery.
fields.interpretation_hints: Strongly negative (<-0.15) → vegetation loss; investigate for fire, drought, or land conversion. Strongly positive (>+0.15) → recovery or new growth.
fields.name: ndvi_change_5y

fields.description: USDA Cropland Data Layer class name at the queried point — a crop (Corn, Soybeans, Cotton, Winter Wheat, …) OR a non-crop CDL land-cover class (Developed, Open Water, Deciduous Forest, Grassland/Pasture, …). NULL only when the point is outside the CDL CONUS grid or on a background/nodata cell. Pair with is_cultivated to distinguish cultivated cropland from non-crop cover.
fields.interpretation_hints: A populated value is NOT necessarily a crop — it may be a non-crop cover class (e.g. Developed, Open Water, Forest); check is_cultivated to tell them apart. NULL means the point is outside the CDL CONUS footprint or a nodata cell — NOT 'not on cropland'.
fields.name: cdl_class
fields.null_meaning: Point is outside the CDL CONUS grid or on a background/nodata cell — no CDL class at this location.

fields.description: True if the queried point is on USDA-mapped cultivated cropland.
fields.interpretation_hints: A NULL is distinct from False — null means the point is outside the CDL CONUS grid or on a background/nodata cell (cultivation unknown), whereas False means CDL positively classifies it as non-cultivated (urban, forest, water). Never read a null as 'not cultivated'.
fields.name: is_cultivated
fields.null_meaning: Point is outside the CDL CONUS grid footprint or on a background/nodata cell — cultivation is unknown here, NOT necessarily uncultivated.

fields.description: Most-frequent crop classification over the last 5 CDL years at the queried point. Helps see past 1-year rotation noise.
fields.interpretation_hints: For 'what's the dominant crop' questions, prefer this over the single-year cdl_class — it smooths over corn-soy rotation.
fields.name: dominant_crop_5y
fields.null_meaning: Not enough cultivated crop history or point is not cropland.

fields.description: Height in meters of the building containing (or nearest to) the queried point, from Overture Buildings.
fields.interpretation_hints: Tall buildings (>20m) suggest commercial / mid-rise context. Combine with primary_building_overture_class and primary_building_footprint_sqm to characterise the structure.
fields.name: primary_building_height_m
fields.null_meaning: No Overture building was found within the query radius, or the building carries no height tag. Untagged does NOT mean the building is flat or single-storey - Overture records only what the upstream source tagged.

fields.description: Number of floors of the primary building at/near the queried point.
fields.name: primary_building_num_floors
fields.null_meaning: No Overture building was found within the query radius, or the building carries no num_floors tag. Untagged does NOT mean one floor; most Overture buildings have no floor count at all.

fields.description: Building footprint area in square meters from Overture Buildings.
fields.name: primary_building_footprint_sqm
fields.null_meaning: No Overture building was found within the query radius. Footprint area is derived from the geometry, so a building that is found always has one.

fields.description: Overture-classified building category (residential / commercial / industrial / civic / etc.) of the primary building.
fields.interpretation_hints: Use to determine 'what kind of building is here'. Combine with primary_building_height_m / num_floors / footprint_sqm for a fuller description.
fields.name: primary_building_overture_class
fields.null_meaning: No Overture building was found within the query radius, or the building carries no class label. Untagged does NOT mean the structure is unclassifiable - it means the upstream source did not label it.

fields.description: Name of the nearest major road (motorway / trunk / primary / secondary) from Overture Roads.
fields.name: nearest_major_road_name
fields.null_meaning: No Overture major road was found within the fallback search radius.

fields.description: Geodesic distance to the nearest major road in meters.
fields.name: nearest_major_road_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No Overture major road was found within the fallback search radius.

fields.description: Name of the nearest FHWA-NBI catalogued bridge.
fields.name: nearest_bridge_name
fields.null_meaning: No NBI bridge was found within the query radius, or the nearest bridge's FACILITY_CARRIED_007 column is blank in the NBI record.

fields.description: Name of the nearest electric power-generating facility (EIA Atlas).
fields.interpretation_hints: The TRUE nearest EIA-registered generator, which is often NOT grid generation — in a downtown it is frequently an office/hospital/campus generator registered under the building's name (e.g. 'Bank of America Plaza'). ALWAYS read nearest_power_plant_sector alongside it - 'Electric Utility' / 'IPP CHP' / 'IPP Non-CHP' are EIA's electric power sector; 'Commercial *' / 'Industrial *' are generation primarily serving the host site. Pair with nearest_power_plant_distance_m, _primary_fuel, _capacity_mw and _technology for a complete answer to 'tell me about the nearest power plant'.
fields.name: nearest_power_plant_name

fields.description: Geodesic distance in meters to the nearest EIA Atlas power plant.
fields.interpretation_hints: Distance to the TRUE nearest EIA-registered generator of any kind, INCLUDING behind-the-meter ones — never read it alone as 'grid generation is this close'. Check nearest_power_plant_sector first; a commercial/industrial sector plant is generation for the host site, not grid supply you can contract. <1000m → significant noise / emissions proximity for residential due diligence. <50km is typically considered 'in range' for grid integration, but only for an electric-power-sector plant.
fields.name: nearest_power_plant_distance_m

fields.description: Primary fuel of the nearest power plant (Natural Gas, Coal, Nuclear, Solar, Wind, Hydro, etc.).
fields.interpretation_hints: The fuel of whatever plant is nearest — which may be a behind-the-meter generator, so 'petroleum' at an urban coordinate is usually a building's on-site engine rather than an oil-fired power station. Read nearest_power_plant_sector + _capacity_mw before characterising the local generation mix from this one field; for the area's real fuel mix use egrid_subregion.
fields.name: nearest_power_plant_primary_fuel

fields.description: Summer (net) generating capacity in megawatts of the nearest power plant, as published by the EIA Atlas — typically ~10% below nameplate capacity. Do not treat as nameplate.
fields.interpretation_hints: Capacity of the nearest plant, NOT of nearby grid supply, and NOT capacity available to a new load (that is an interconnection study). Small values are ambiguous on their own — a 2.6 MW petroleum plant in a downtown is usually an on-site engine, while a 0.5 MW Electric Utility plant in rural Alaska is the village's entire grid — read nearest_power_plant_sector to tell them apart. Large values are ambiguous too - the largest behind-the-meter installations in EIA-860 exceed 90 MW.
fields.name: nearest_power_plant_capacity_mw

fields.description: Distance in meters to the nearest EIA Atlas transmission line.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_distance_m

fields.description: Operating voltage (kV) of the single nearest EIA/HIFLD transmission line. Null when the source publishes no numeric voltage for that segment.
fields.interpretation_hints: Voltage of the CLOSEST line — may be lower than max_transmission_line_voltage_kv_within_radius if a higher-voltage line runs slightly farther; read both. >=230 kV = transmission-grade, <100 kV = sub-transmission. Pair with nearest_transmission_line_distance_m (tap distance). Null here != 'no voltage' — check nearest_transmission_line_voltage_class / _basis. Never infer substation capacity from this.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_voltage_kv

fields.description: Voltage-class band of the nearest line (e.g. "100-161", "345", "500") from source VOLT_CLASS. A range, not a point value.
fields.interpretation_hints: Use as the voltage signal when nearest_transmission_line_voltage_kv is null (numeric masked). Report as a RANGE ('100-161 kV class'); never collapse a band to a single kV. 'DC' = HVDC. Read with nearest_transmission_line_voltage_basis.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_voltage_class

fields.description: How the nearest line's voltage is known: numeric, class_band, or not_published.
fields.interpretation_hints: Read this BEFORE quoting voltage. numeric -> cite ..._voltage_kv. class_band -> cite ..._voltage_class as a range, do NOT state a precise kV. not_published -> say voltage is not published in the federal source for this segment; do not guess. ~9% of US segments are not_published. This is the honesty contract for voltage.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_voltage_basis

fields.description: Operating status of the nearest line: "IN SERVICE", "UNDER CONSTRUCTION", "INACTIVE", or null when unpublished.
fields.interpretation_hints: Do NOT assume a nearby line is energized — only ~78% are marked IN SERVICE and many real lines have null status. Flag UNDER CONSTRUCTION / INACTIVE explicitly; null = unstated, not 'in service'.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_status

fields.description: Owner/operator of the nearest line (e.g. "ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY CO.") from source OWNER; null when unpublished.
fields.interpretation_hints: The utility to contact for interconnection on the nearest line. Currently the best available utility signal: service_territory_holder is always null until a post-HIFLD successor source for service territories exists.
fields.name: nearest_transmission_line_owner

fields.description: Highest NUMERIC operating voltage (kV) among all transmission lines within ~2 km (transmission_lines_radius_m). Null when no in-range line publishes a numeric voltage.
fields.interpretation_hints: The headline 'is high-voltage transmission adjacent' signal for large-load / data-center siting; >=230 kV strong, 345/500 kV transmission-grade. Highest NUMERIC kV — a class-band-only line could be higher, so ALWAYS read max_transmission_line_voltage_class_within_radius alongside. Pair with nearest_transmission_line_distance_m. For powered-land buyers this confirms grid context, not a capacity claim.
fields.name: max_transmission_line_voltage_kv_within_radius

fields.description: Highest voltage-class band among all lines within ~2 km, ranking class-band-only lines alongside numeric ones. Always >= the band implied by max_transmission_line_voltage_kv_within_radius.
fields.interpretation_hints: The honest 'highest voltage present' signal — captures a high-voltage line even when its numeric kV is masked, so it never understates adjacency. Report as a class/range. If it exceeds the band implied by the numeric max, a higher-voltage line exists whose exact kV the source didn't publish — say so rather than quoting the numeric max as the ceiling.
fields.name: max_transmission_line_voltage_class_within_radius

fields.description: Count of EIA/HIFLD transmission segments within ~2 km (transmission_lines_radius_m).
fields.interpretation_hints: Density of nearby transmission. 0 = none within ~2 km (a siting flag for power-search use cases). Combine with the voltage fields to characterize how much and how high-voltage the nearby grid is.
fields.name: transmission_lines_within_radius_count

fields.description: Distance in meters to the nearest EIA interstate natural-gas pipeline.
fields.interpretation_hints: Also a secondary long-haul-fiber ROW proxy — long-haul fiber commonly shares gas-transmission pipeline rights-of-way (InterTubes, SIGCOMM 2015); combine with nearest_long_haul_rail_corridor_distance_m + nearest_submarine_cable_distance_m.
fields.name: nearest_gas_pipeline_distance_m

fields.description: Name of the EPA SDWIS public water system serving the queried point.
fields.name: nearest_public_water_system_name
fields.null_meaning: No large community water system (>10,000 served) in the point's state, the point is outside the US state grid, or the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending / corrupt asset).

fields.description: Distance in meters to the nearest BTS NTAD rail line within a 5 km search; null if none within 5 km.
fields.interpretation_hints: Distance to the nearest rail line of ANY class (incl. spurs/yards) — a coarse ROW-corridor signal. null = no rail line within 5 km (NOT 'no rail anywhere' — the search is capped at 5 km), which is a valid no-data answer, not a failure. For a long-haul-fiber-capable corridor prefer the mainline-filtered nearest_long_haul_rail_corridor_distance_m.
fields.name: nearest_rail_line_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No BTS NTAD rail line within the 5 km search radius (NOT 'no rail anywhere' — the search is capped at 5 km).

fields.description: Name of the nearest FAA NASR airport.
fields.name: nearest_airport_name

fields.description: Distance in meters to the nearest FAA NASR airport.
fields.name: nearest_airport_distance_m

fields.description: Name of the nearest BTS Principal Port.
fields.name: nearest_port_name

fields.description: Geodesic distance in meters to the nearest FCC-registered antenna structure within a 2 km buffer. Source is the FCC ULS Antenna Structure Registration (ASR), which only includes structures >=200 ft AGL (FAA Form 7460 threshold); small cells and sub-threshold towers are not in the federal index.
fields.interpretation_hints: Distance <500m → likely RF / line-of-sight considerations for tall builds. Null distance with non-zero antenna_structures_within_2km_count is impossible; null with zero count means the buffer is empty. See fcc_asr_note for the sub-200ft caveat.
fields.name: nearest_antenna_structure_distance_m

fields.description: Overall height above ground (in meters) of the nearest FCC ASR antenna structure. Always >=60.96 m by construction.
fields.name: nearest_antenna_structure_height_m

fields.description: FCC structure-type code for the nearest antenna structure (e.g. BTWR = building-mounted tower, BANT = antenna on building, TOWER = freestanding tower, GTOWER = guyed tower).
fields.name: nearest_antenna_structure_type

fields.description: FCC ASR registration number of the nearest antenna structure. Cross-reference https://wireless2.fcc.gov/UlsApp/AsrSearch/ for the registrant entity.
fields.name: nearest_antenna_structure_owner

fields.description: Count of FCC ASR antenna structures within 500 m of the queried point. Dense urban clusters (broadcast row, downtown rooftops) typically register multiple structures inside this radius.
fields.name: antenna_structures_within_500m_count

fields.description: Count of FCC ASR antenna structures within the 2 km query buffer. Zero count means no registered tall antennas within 2 km.
fields.name: antenna_structures_within_2km_count

fields.description: US state name from Overture Divisions at the queried point.
fields.name: political_region

fields.description: County name from Overture Divisions at the queried point.
fields.name: political_county

fields.description: Locality / city name from Overture Divisions.
fields.name: political_locality

fields.description: US Census tract GEOID (11 digits: STATE+COUNTY+TRACT) containing the queried point.
fields.name: tract_geoid

fields.description: True if the queried point intersects a USGS PAD-US 4.1 conservation easement. PAD-US is the federal aggregation of conservation easements after NCED was discontinued in 2025.
fields.interpretation_hints: True → check easement_holder/purpose/acres for the encumbrance details. Conservation easements restrict development; relevant for 'can I build here' questions.
fields.name: intersects_conservation_easement

fields.description: Holder organization of the intersecting conservation easement.
fields.name: easement_holder
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US conservation easement intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Type/category of the intersecting PAD-US conservation easement.
fields.interpretation_hints: Detail of the conservation easement at the point. An encumbrance to verify by title search (see other_easements_note); a recorded easement restricts but does not necessarily forbid development.
fields.name: easement_type
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US conservation easement intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Stated purpose of the intersecting easement. PAD-US 4.1 publishes no stated-purpose attribute for easement records, so this is null (semantic absence) even when an easement is present.
fields.name: easement_purpose
fields.null_meaning: Either no PAD-US easement intersects this coordinate, or an easement is present but PAD-US 4.1 exposes no stated-purpose attribute.

fields.description: Total GIS acreage of the PAD-US conservation easement polygon intersecting the point — NOT the share of any parcel.
fields.interpretation_hints: This is the whole mapped easement's size, which routinely spans many properties and may extend far beyond a given site. Do NOT present it as 'easement on this parcel' — a 5,000-acre easement clipping the corner of a 200-acre parcel reports 5000 here. On-site coverage is easement_acres_on_parcel / easement_fraction_of_parcel (parcels layer, needs a matched Regrid parcel). Use this for 'how large is the easement here', not 'how much of my land is encumbered'.
fields.name: easement_acres
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US conservation easement intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Year the intersecting PAD-US conservation easement was established.
fields.name: easement_year_established
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US conservation easement intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: True if the queried point intersects a USGS PAD-US 4.1 protected area (Fee or Designation): parks, refuges, wilderness, military, NGO preserves.
fields.interpretation_hints: PAD-US (USGS GAP) describes public-land ownership/management intent, NOT buildability — a private target parcel will NOT appear here. Read protected_area_gap_status: 1 strict (wilderness/park core), 2 protected (refuge/state park), 3 multiple-use, 4 ~ nominal (city parks/military — minimal real constraint). Pair with protected_area_designation + protected_area_manager. The reported unit is the MOST protective (lowest GAP) of any overlapping polygons.
fields.name: intersects_protected_area

fields.description: Name of the intersecting PAD-US protected area (most protective unit).
fields.name: protected_area_name
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US protected area intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: GAP status (1–4) of the intersecting PAD-US protected area — the conservation-strictness axis.
fields.interpretation_hints: GAP 1–4 strictness. 1/2 = real conservation protection (wilderness, park core, refuge, state park); 3 = protected from conversion but extractive uses allowed; 4 ~ nominal — no mandate to prevent conversion (city parks, military). Do NOT overstate GAP 4 as a development constraint.
fields.name: protected_area_gap_status
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US protected area intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Designation type (Wilderness/Refuge/Park…) of the intersecting protected area.
fields.interpretation_hints: The interpretive payload alongside protected_area_gap_status / protected_area_manager; the bare intersection alone is not 'undevelopable'.
fields.name: protected_area_designation
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US protected area intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Managing entity of the intersecting PAD-US protected area.
fields.name: protected_area_manager
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US protected area intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: Public-access level (Open/Restricted/Closed/Unknown) of the protected area.
fields.name: protected_area_public_access
fields.null_meaning: No PAD-US protected area intersects this coordinate.

fields.description: True if the queried point intersects USFWS ESA-designated critical habitat (Final OR Proposed polygon).
fields.interpretation_hints: USFWS ESA-designated critical habitat. Designation does NOT prohibit development on private land; it triggers ESA §7 consultation ONLY with a federal nexus (federal funding/permit/action) likely to adversely modify it. NEVER say 'cannot be developed' or 'ESA-blocked'. Designation ≠ species present (unoccupied areas are designated). Read critical_habitat_status — Final vs Proposed is regulatory vs not. A clean result ≠ clean ESA (species range / IPaC is broader), and the linear habitat layers are not queried.
fields.name: intersects_critical_habitat

fields.description: Designation status of the intersecting critical habitat: Final or Proposed.
fields.interpretation_hints: Final = legally designated, carries the §7 'destroy/adversely modify' prohibition for federal actions. Proposed = no regulatory effect yet (confer, not consult). NEVER treat Proposed as a binding constraint, and never collapse Final vs Proposed.
fields.name: critical_habitat_status
fields.null_meaning: No USFWS critical habitat (Final or Proposed) intersects this coordinate, or a local USFWS critical-habitat asset (Final/Proposed gpkg) is missing/corrupt.

fields.description: Listed species (common + scientific name) the critical habitat is designated for.
fields.interpretation_hints: The listed species the habitat is designated for. Habitat for an unlisted species is not designated; absence ≠ no sensitive habitat.
fields.name: critical_habitat_species
fields.null_meaning: No USFWS critical habitat (Final or Proposed) intersects this coordinate, or a local USFWS critical-habitat asset (Final/Proposed gpkg) is missing/corrupt.

fields.description: ESA listing status (Endangered/Threatened) of the critical-habitat species.
fields.name: critical_habitat_listing_status
fields.null_meaning: No USFWS critical habitat (Final or Proposed) intersects this coordinate, or a local USFWS critical-habitat asset (Final/Proposed gpkg) is missing/corrupt.

fields.description: WKT polygon of the matched Regrid parcel (WGS84). POLYGON only — for a multi-polygon parcel use parcel_boundary_geojson, which keeps every part.
fields.interpretation_hints: The single parcel polygon at the point (WGS84), NOT the assembled holding — a multi-parcel site (e.g. a ranch) is a union of many parcels. Pair with parcel_match_type: an exact hit is the parcel under the point; a nearest-fallback (nearest_within_radius) is the closest parcel within parcel_match_radius_m, NOT necessarily the one at the point. Use for site footprint/acreage; assemble multi-parcel holdings separately.
fields.name: parcel_geometry_wkt
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon of the matched Regrid parcel (WGS84) as a JSON string; json.loads it. Preserves MultiPolygon parts that parcel_geometry_wkt truncates.
fields.interpretation_hints: The single parcel polygon at the point (WGS84), NOT the assembled holding — a multi-parcel site (e.g. a ranch) is a union of many parcels. Pair with parcel_match_type: an exact hit is the parcel under the point; a nearest-fallback (nearest_within_radius) is the closest parcel within parcel_match_radius_m, NOT necessarily the one at the point. Use for site footprint/acreage; assemble multi-parcel holdings separately.
fields.name: parcel_boundary_geojson
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Stable Regrid identifier for the matched parcel.
fields.interpretation_hints: Ownership/identity reflect the Regrid source vintage, which can predate a recent sale — verify recent transactions (a parcel may still list a prior owner after acquisition). parcel_data_source tells you the tier; premium fields are null on regrid_free_tier (data-tier limited, NOT 'no parcel here').
fields.name: parcel_id
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Assessor's parcel number (APN) for the matched parcel.
fields.interpretation_hints: Ownership/identity reflect the Regrid source vintage, which can predate a recent sale — verify recent transactions (a parcel may still list a prior owner after acquisition). parcel_data_source tells you the tier; premium fields are null on regrid_free_tier (data-tier limited, NOT 'no parcel here').
fields.name: parcel_apn
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Area of the single matched Regrid parcel in square meters, derived from Regrid's calculated acreage (ll_gisacre) or square footage (ll_gissqft) — Regrid's US schema has no metric area column — falling back to county-provided gisacre/sqft.
fields.interpretation_hints: Area of the single matched parcel in m². For a multi-parcel site, sum across parcels. Cross-check against parcel_geometry_wkt / parcel_boundary_geojson. Null when the county supplies no area column (coverage varies), not when there is no parcel.
fields.name: parcel_area_m2
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Situs/site address of the matched Regrid parcel, when present.
fields.name: parcel_address
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Which Regrid tier produced this parcel: regrid_paid or regrid_free_tier.
fields.interpretation_hints: regrid_paid (premium fields populated) vs regrid_free_tier (geometry/id only; owner/zoning/value null = UNKNOWN, not absent).
fields.name: parcel_data_source
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Owner of record for the exact Regrid parcel at the queried point, or for the bounded nearest parcel when an exact point lookup misses.
fields.interpretation_hints: Ownership reflects the Regrid source vintage, which can predate a recent sale — verify recent transactions (a parcel may still list a prior owner after acquisition). parcel_data_source tells you the tier; premium fields are null on regrid_free_tier (data-tier limited, NOT 'no parcel here').
fields.name: parcel_owner
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel was found at the point or within the bounded nearest-parcel radius, or the returned parcel lacks owner data.

fields.description: Zoning designation for the exact Regrid parcel at the queried point, or for the bounded nearest parcel when an exact point lookup misses.
fields.interpretation_hints: Zoning is the load-bearing answer for 'can I build here' questions. Read from the matched Regrid parcel's base attributes; null when no parcel matches the point (or bounded nearest-parcel radius) or the matched parcel carries no zoning designation.
fields.name: parcel_zoning
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel was found at the point or within the bounded nearest-parcel radius, or the returned parcel lacks zoning data.

fields.description: How the Regrid parcel was matched: exact_intersect for point-in-parcel matches, or nearest_within_radius for bounded fallback matches.
fields.name: parcel_match_type
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel was found at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Distance from the query point to the selected Regrid parcel geometry; 0 for exact point-in-parcel matches.
fields.name: parcel_match_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel was found at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Configured Regrid nearest-parcel fallback radius used for this match; 0 for exact point-in-parcel matches.
fields.name: parcel_match_radius_m
fields.null_meaning: No Regrid parcel was found at the point or within the bounded radius.

fields.description: Annual-average global horizontal irradiance at the point, sampled from the NREL PSM v3 multiyear (1998-2016) ~4 km solar-resource raster (local index; no API key needed).
fields.interpretation_hints: >5.0 = premium (SW desert); 4.0-5.0 workable; <3.8 (Pacific NW/NE) materially erodes economics. First-pass solar go/no-go before any yield model.
fields.name: ghi_annual_kwh_m2_day
fields.null_meaning: Outside the PSM v3 Americas grid footprint, on a nodata cell, or the local raster asset is unavailable.

fields.description: Annual-average direct normal (beam) irradiance, sampled from the NREL PSM v3 multiyear (1998-2016) ~4 km solar-resource raster (local index; no API key needed). Drives CSP and tracking-system economics.
fields.interpretation_hints: CSP only viable above ~6.0 (AZ/NV/S.CA). High DNI relative to GHI signals strong single-axis-tracking upside; low DNI (humid SE) favors fixed-tilt.
fields.name: dni_annual_kwh_m2_day
fields.null_meaning: Outside the PSM v3 Americas grid footprint, on a nodata cell, or the local raster asset is unavailable.

fields.description: Modeled first-year AC capacity factor for a fixed-tilt open-rack PV system, from NREL PVWatts v8 (latitude tilt, south-facing).
fields.interpretation_hints: ~15% (cloudy N) to ~26% (SW desert); a 2-3 pt swing moves LCOE and PPA pricing materially. Modeled value — config recorded in provenance.
fields.name: pv_capacity_factor_pct
fields.null_meaning: NREL key not configured or PVWatts fetch failed.

fields.description: Modeled annual AC energy per kW-DC installed (ac_annual / system_capacity) for a fixed-tilt system, from NREL PVWatts v8.
fields.interpretation_hints: US ~1,300 (cold N) to ~1,900 (SW). Ranks parcels by expected $/installed-W return without a full energy model.
fields.name: pv_specific_yield_kwh_per_kw
fields.null_meaning: NREL key not configured or PVWatts fetch failed.

fields.description: Energy-maximising fixed array tilt. Reported as the latitude rule-of-thumb (|lat|); exact optimum is within a few degrees (see provenance notes).
fields.interpretation_hints: Rises with latitude (~20deg S.TX to ~40deg upper Midwest); drives row spacing / GCR and land-area-per-MW. Array geometry only — distinct from terrain slope_degrees.
fields.name: optimal_fixed_tilt_degrees
fields.null_meaning: Always populated — the latitude rule-of-thumb (|lat|) is computed in-process, independent of the NREL key and the PVWatts fetch; null only if the entire solar_resource layer fails to return.

fields.description: Dimensionless 0-1 broadband ground albedo (annual mean), from the NREL NSRDB GOES TMY series. Drives bifacial PV rear-side gain.
fields.interpretation_hints: High (snow ~0.6+, desert ~0.25-0.35) adds 5-15% bifacial rear-side yield; low (dark soil/veg ~0.15) erodes the bifacial case.
fields.name: surface_albedo_annual
fields.null_meaning: No NREL key or NSRDB contact email, NSRDB GOES-TMY fetch failed/timed out, or outside coverage.

fields.description: Long-term annual-mean wind speed at 100m hub height (NREL WIND Toolkit, 2 km CONUS, 2007-2014 climatology).
fields.interpretation_hints: <6 marginal, 6.5-7.5 workable, >7.5-8 strong. Largest single driver of wind yield (~v^3). CONUS only.
fields.name: mean_wind_speed_100m_ms
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Annual-mean wind speed at 120m (current-generation hub height), NREL WIND Toolkit.
fields.interpretation_hints: Delta vs 100m reads wind shear, used to value taller-tower options. CONUS only.
fields.name: mean_wind_speed_120m_ms
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Annual-mean wind speed at 160m (tall-tower/repowering height), NREL WIND Toolkit.
fields.interpretation_hints: With 100m/120m lets a selector compute the vertical shear exponent (alpha) and decide if a taller tower pays off. CONUS only.
fields.name: mean_wind_speed_160m_ms
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Mean wind power density at 100m (time-mean of 0.5*rho*v^3), the canonical resource grade. NREL WIND Toolkit-derived.
fields.interpretation_hints: At 100m: <300 poor, 400-500 good, >600 outstanding. CONUS only.
fields.name: wind_power_density_100m_wm2
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: 16-point modal wind-from sector (energy-weighted) at 100m, NREL WIND Toolkit.
fields.interpretation_hints: Drives turbine row orientation, intra-array wake losses, and which neighbor parcels see wake/noise. CONUS only.
fields.name: prevailing_wind_direction_100m_cardinal
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Weibull shape parameter k of the 100m wind-speed distribution, NREL WIND Toolkit.
fields.interpretation_hints: Low k (~1.5-1.8) = gusty/variable (raises fatigue load); high k (~2.5-3) = steady. Shape (not just mean) drives AEP and IEC turbine class. CONUS only.
fields.name: weibull_k_100m
fields.null_meaning: WIND Toolkit grid not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Modeled mean capacity factor of a reference 115m-hub / 170m-rotor turbine at the nearest NREL reV land-based supply-curve point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Onshore CONUS ~25% (marginal) to ~50%+ (best plains/ridges); a 5-pt swing moves LCOE materially. CONUS only.
fields.name: wind_capacity_factor_pct
fields.null_meaning: reV supply-curve index not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: NREL reV modeled least-cost spur distance from the nearest supply-curve point to the nearest available substation.
fields.interpretation_hints: Basis for levelized cost of transmission. Complements nearest_transmission_line_distance_m (a line is not an injection point). CONUS only.
fields.name: wind_least_cost_interconnect_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: reV supply-curve index not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: TMY-based approximation of the 0.4% cooling design wet-bulb: the 99.6th percentile of hourly wet-bulb over one NREL NSRDB GOES-TMY year, solved psychrometrically from dry-bulb + dew-point. A single typical year clips extremes, so this runs slightly cool of the true multi-year ASHRAE design value (reported at medium confidence).
fields.interpretation_hints: THE variable for evaporative-cooling viability: >~25C = low evap potential (oversize towers, less water saving); low = water-side economization + lower cooling capex. TMY approximation, not the certified ASHRAE design condition.
fields.name: design_wet_bulb_temperature_0_4pct_degc
fields.null_meaning: No NREL key or NSRDB contact email, NSRDB GOES-TMY fetch failed/timed out, or outside coverage.

fields.description: Mean annual dry-bulb air temperature from NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 gridded normals (~4.6 km). CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: Baseline for data-center cooling-energy and PV cell-temp derate (PV output drops ~0.3-0.5%/C above 25C). CONUS only (no AK/HI).
fields.name: mean_annual_dry_bulb_temperature_degc
fields.null_meaning: NCEI normals raster not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Mean annual relative humidity, the mean of the hourly RH column from the same NREL NSRDB GOES-TMY series the design wet-bulb is derived from (one fetch, one climatology, self-consistent).
fields.interpretation_hints: With dry-bulb sets wet-bulb depression: low RH (arid) = excellent low-water adiabatic/evaporative cooling; high RH (humid) loses evap effectiveness.
fields.name: mean_annual_relative_humidity_pct
fields.null_meaning: No NREL key or NSRDB contact email, NSRDB GOES-TMY fetch failed/timed out, or outside coverage.

fields.description: Mean days/yr with Tmax >= 32C (90F), from NOAA NCEI nClimGrid-Daily (~5 km) averaged across years. CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: Quantifies how often cooling runs at peak and PV/transformer thermal-derate days occur. CONUS only.
fields.name: days_above_32c_annual_count
fields.null_meaning: nClimGrid-Daily raster not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: Mean annual snow-cover days from the NSIDC-0791 MODIS/Terra 0.01deg snow-cover-duration climatology (WY2001-2023). CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: High counts (upper Midwest/Mountain West) argue steeper snow-shedding PV tilt and add winter production loss / O&M cost. MODIS-derived (the correct-definition counterpart to the intractable ~200GB raw SNODAS). CONUS only.
fields.name: mean_annual_snow_cover_days
fields.null_meaning: MODIS snow-cover-duration climatology not bootstrapped, or outside CONUS.

fields.description: ASCE 7-22 Seismic Design Category (A-F) from the USGS design-maps web service. Site class is assumed D (code default); recorded in provenance.
fields.interpretation_hints: A/B minimal detailing; D/E/F require special seismic systems + equipment certification + major cost/schedule. Re-query with a real site class once geotech is known.
fields.name: seismic_design_category
fields.null_meaning: Outside the design-maps domain or the service fetch failed.

fields.description: Peak ground acceleration at 2% exceedance in 50yr (~2475-yr return), firm-rock VS30=760, from the USGS 2023 NSHM. CONUS only.
fields.interpretation_hints: >~0.4g flags high-cost seismic design/anchorage for racks, transformers, battery enclosures, turbine foundations; <~0.1g benign. CONUS only.
fields.name: seismic_pga_2pct_50yr_g
fields.null_meaning: Outside the served NSHM CONUS grid footprint or on a no-data cell, or the raster is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: ASCE 7-22 basic design wind speed (3-second gust, Risk Category II / 700-yr MRI, Exposure C) from NOAA's free CC0 mirror of the ASCE wind vectors.
fields.interpretation_hints: The structural-design input for PV racking, turbine towers, and building envelopes. Banded mph. Use the free NOAA layer, not the gated ASCE tool.
fields.name: design_wind_speed_mph
fields.null_meaning: The point is outside the mapped ASCE wind-vector domain (offshore / out-of-coverage), or the local NOAA ASCE wind asset is missing/corrupt (or a containing band carried no usable gridcode).

fields.description: Annualized wildfire event frequency (events/yr) for the containing Census tract, from FEMA National Risk Index (WFIR_AFREQ).
fields.interpretation_hints: A top western insurability / total-loss gate for utility PV and wind, and a data-center business-continuity input. National.
fields.name: wildfire_annual_frequency
fields.null_meaning: Null when the point resolves to no US Census tract, the tract is absent from the local NRI table, this frequency is not tabulated for the tract, or the live tract resolve / local table read failed.

fields.description: Annualized tornado event frequency (events/yr) for the containing Census tract, from FEMA NRI (TRND_AFREQ).
fields.interpretation_hints: Ranks Tornado Alley vs low-risk basins; informs hardened-enclosure / impact glazing.
fields.name: tornado_annual_frequency
fields.null_meaning: Null when the point resolves to no US Census tract, the tract is absent from the local NRI table, this frequency is not tabulated for the tract, or the live tract resolve / local table read failed.

fields.description: Annualized hail event frequency (events/yr) for the containing Census tract, from FEMA NRI (HAIL_AFREQ).
fields.interpretation_hints: Hail is the single largest utility-PV insurance-loss cause; drives module hail-rating (stow-capable trackers, glass thickness) and insurer pricing.
fields.name: hail_annual_frequency
fields.null_meaning: Null when the point resolves to no US Census tract, the tract is absent from the local NRI table, this frequency is not tabulated for the tract, or the live tract resolve / local table read failed.

fields.description: Estimated lightning days per year for the containing Census tract, from FEMA NRI (LTNG_AFREQ; days/yr, not flash count).
fields.interpretation_hints: Drives surge-protection, grounding, and inverter/transformer transient-protection scope.
fields.name: lightning_annual_flash_days
fields.null_meaning: Null when the point resolves to no US Census tract, the tract is absent from the local NRI table, this frequency is not tabulated for the tract, or the live tract resolve / local table read failed.

fields.description: USGS Slope-Relief-Threshold landslide susceptibility (0-81 = count of susceptible 10 m cells in the 90 m cell). National.
fields.interpretation_hints: High values trigger geotech investigation for foundations / access roads / buried interconnect on slopes. Complements slope_degrees (modeled failure, not just steepness).
fields.name: landslide_susceptibility_index
fields.null_meaning: Outside the served CONUS + Puerto Rico envelope or a no-data cell, or the raster is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Straight-line distance to the nearest dam in the USACE National Inventory of Dams, searched within a 10 km screening band.
fields.interpretation_hints: Proximity is a screening signal, not inundation exposure — flow direction and topography decide that; request the dam's EAP/inundation map via the state dam-safety office. Combine with nearest_dam_hazard_potential and the flood-zone fields.
fields.name: nearest_dam_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No NID dam within 10 km (a semantic absence), or the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: USACE hazard-potential class of the nearest NID dam (High / Significant / Low / Undetermined).
fields.interpretation_hints: A consequence-of-failure class (High = probable loss of life if the dam failed) — NOT a condition or failure-probability rating; many dams' condition assessments are access-restricted. High/Significant nearby → ask for the Emergency Action Plan.
fields.name: nearest_dam_hazard_potential
fields.null_meaning: No NID dam within 10 km, or the nearest dam's hazard class is blank in source; a failed read means the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Count of High hazard-potential NID dams within 10 km of the point.
fields.interpretation_hints: A floor — small dams below the NID inventory threshold are not counted. Zero High-hazard dams does not mean zero dams; see nearest_dam_distance_m.
fields.name: high_hazard_dams_within_10km
fields.null_meaning: The local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending); a successful empty radius returns 0.

fields.description: Distance to the nearest EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) facility geocode in the Facility Registry Service, searched within 10 km.
fields.interpretation_hints: RMP registration means regulated chemicals on site — read it as 'check what this facility is', never as danger. Explosives were delisted from RMP in 1998 and ammonium nitrate is not listed, so the worst neighbor may be absent; FRS also retains ever-registered (possibly closed) facilities and geocode accuracy varies. Combine with nearest_hazardous_facility_name.
fields.name: nearest_hazardous_facility_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No RMP facility within 10 km, or the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending / corrupt asset).

fields.description: EPA FRS primary name of the nearest RMP-registered facility (upstream casing preserved).
fields.interpretation_hints: The name is the lead for due diligence — look the facility up before characterizing it; the registry says a regulated process exists, not what condition it is in. Combine with nearest_hazardous_facility_distance_m.
fields.name: nearest_hazardous_facility_name
fields.null_meaning: No RMP facility within 10 km, the nearest facility carries no usable name, or the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending / corrupt asset).

fields.description: 2020 Census housing units across blocks intersecting a 1 km band around the point (TIGERweb tabblock HU100; edge blocks counted whole).
fields.interpretation_hints: A community-pushback exposure proxy, not sentiment. 2020 vintage — post-2020 construction is absent, which understates exactly the fast-growing exurban areas; edge-block whole-counting biases high. Combine with housing_units_density_per_km2.
fields.name: housing_units_within_1km
fields.null_meaning: Point outside US Census block coverage (not tagged as tabulated US territory), or the query failed. A successful in-coverage empty band returns 0.

fields.description: Housing units per km2 of block land area within the 1 km band (water excluded from the denominator), from 2020 Census blocks.
fields.interpretation_hints: Anchors: Census urban criteria ~164 units/km2 (assume organized pushback); rural <6.2, exurban 6.2-147, suburban 147-1,000, urban >1,000 (Theobald bands). A pushback-exposure proxy on 2020 data, not sentiment. Combine with housing_units_within_1km and nearest_urban_area_distance_m.
fields.name: housing_units_density_per_km2
fields.null_meaning: All intersecting blocks are water-only (no land area in the band), the point is outside US Census block coverage, or the query failed.

fields.description: Great-circle distance to the nearest electric substation (EIA Atlas, >=69kV layer), the physical interconnection injection point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Interconnection cost scales with gen-tie/feeder distance: within a few km is materially cheaper/faster; >10-20km often kills a site. A substation is the injection point — complements nearest_transmission_line_distance_m (a line is not).
fields.name: nearest_substation_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No substation within the search radius, or the local substation index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Maximum voltage (MAX_VOLT) of the nearest electric substation, from EIA Atlas.
fields.interpretation_hints: Higher (230/345/500 vs 69/115) signals more headroom to absorb large gen/load; a 69kV-only station may be too weak for 200MW+.
fields.name: nearest_substation_max_voltage_kv
fields.null_meaning: No substation within radius, voltage not published, or the local substation index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Operational status of the nearest substation (e.g. IN SERVICE / UNDER CONST / PROPOSED / NOT AVAILABLE), from EIA Atlas.
fields.interpretation_hints: Confirms the nearby substation is energized/usable vs retired/planned.
fields.name: nearest_substation_status
fields.null_meaning: No substation within radius, status not published, or the local substation index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Name of the retail electric utility whose service territory contains the point. First routing key for interconnection / PPA / tariff.
fields.interpretation_hints: The containing retail-service-territory polygon (DataLumos Electric Retail Service Territories, reduced from the HIFLD/EIA Atlas layer). Identifies the utility to approach for interconnection / PPA / tariff. Territories can overlap for two different reasons and the answer is resolved accordingly: where a retail muni genuinely NESTS inside a broader wholesale coop footprint, the innermost polygon is reported at high confidence, since it really is the direct retail provider. Where the overlap is instead a boundary-digitization defect (the source fills in municipal enclaves rather than cutting holes for them), a municipal utility claiming a point in a DIFFERENT city is not used, and any answer that cannot be confirmed is returned at reduced confidence with the competing utility named in the notes — so treat a non-high confidence here as "confirm with the utility".
fields.name: electric_utility_service_territory
fields.null_meaning: The point falls outside every mapped retail service territory, or the local service-territory index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Most-recent industrial-sector average retail electricity price for the area (EIA; state-level, refinable to utility once territory is known).
fields.interpretation_hints: Dominant data-center opex and a storage-arbitrage input; sub-cent moves siting between low-cost WA/ID and high-cost CA/New England. State aggregate (areal).
fields.name: avg_retail_electricity_price_industrial_usd_per_kwh
fields.null_meaning: Point did not resolve to a U.S. state, or the state is not in the local EIA price table (served from a local per-state table; no API key).

fields.description: EPA eGRID subregion code (e.g. RFCW, CAMX, ERCT) whose polygon contains the point.
fields.interpretation_hints: Standard key for Scope-2 location-based emissions accounting and clean-energy procurement. Boundaries are approximate; near-boundary points may differ from the serving utility.
fields.name: egrid_subregion
fields.null_meaning: Point falls outside any mapped eGRID subregion (semantic absence), or FAILED if the local eGRID asset is missing or corrupt.

fields.description: Annual total-output CO2e rate of the containing eGRID subregion (EPA eGRID).
fields.interpretation_hints: Carbon intensity of the local grid is an underwriting/ESG gate for 24/7-CFE data centers and a storage-arbitrage signal. Subregion aggregate.
fields.name: egrid_co2_output_rate_kg_per_mwh
fields.null_meaning: Point outside any eGRID subregion or no eGRID CO2 rate tabulated for the subregion (semantic absence), or FAILED if the local eGRID asset is missing or corrupt.

fields.description: Total nameplate MW of active-queue generation/storage projects in the containing county (LBNL 'Queued Up', keyed by county FIPS).
fields.interpretation_hints: Heavy active queue = constrained headroom + study-delay risk; low queue near strong transmission = green-field signal. County aggregate, annual snapshot.
fields.name: interconnection_queue_active_capacity_county_mw
fields.null_meaning: No active interconnection-queue project in this county, or the dataset is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Distance to the nearest proposed / under-construction generator (EIA-860M Planned tab). Existing power-plant fields cover operating plants only.
fields.interpretation_hints: A nearby planned unit reveals future injection competing for — or adding — interconnect headroom. Plant-level point.
fields.name: nearest_proposed_generator_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No EIA-860M planned generator within 100 km, or the index is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: USGS surface-water supply-and-use index (0 = no limitation to 1 = total local depletion) for the containing HUC12 watershed.
fields.interpretation_hints: Federal public counterpart to commercial water-risk indices; high SUI flags watersheds where consumptive use approaches supply (permitting/curtailment risk). Lower-48.
fields.name: surface_water_supply_use_index_huc12
fields.null_meaning: No IWAA record for the point's HUC12 (outside CONUS coverage), or the index is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Population served by the EPA community water system whose service-area polygon contains the point.
fields.interpretation_hints: A large CWS more plausibly has headroom for a water-cooled DC's makeup demand; tiny/no CWS means costly self-supply. Complements nearest_public_water_system_name. This is SDWIS "average daily population served", self-reported and lagging, so it can change between EPA editions for an unchanged boundary. The boundary that selected this system may be ML-modeled — check water_service_area_provenance.
fields.name: public_water_system_population_served
fields.null_meaning: No EPA community water system polygon contains the point, the containing system's population-served value is blank or a non-positive placeholder in source, or the local CWS index is unreadable.

fields.description: Existing freshwater thermoelectric consumptive use summed in the containing HUC12, latest full year 2020 (USGS 2008-2020 reanalysis).
fields.interpretation_hints: Quantifies competing heavy water demand a water-cooled DC would contend with; high in-watershed use signals tighter permitting. Overlaps the SUI signal — secondary.
fields.name: huc12_thermoelectric_consumptive_use_m3_per_day
fields.null_meaning: No thermoelectric power plant in the containing HUC12 (semantic absence), or the dataset is not bootstrapped.

fields.description: Depth to water at the nearest USGS NWIS groundwater well (param 72019). Sparse / often a historical reading — use as a coarse indicator.
fields.interpretation_hints: Shallow depth = easier/cheaper on-site wells and reliable cooling makeup; deep/declining = aquifer stress, high pumping cost. Sparse coverage — secondary signal.
fields.name: nearest_groundwater_well_depth_to_water_m
fields.null_meaning: No NWIS groundwater well with depth data near the point, or the NWIS OGC fetch failed.

fields.description: Count of distinct ISPs reporting Fiber-to-the-Premises (FTTP) mass-market availability in the FCC BDC H3 res-8 hexagon containing the point (live ArcGIS Living Atlas mirror).
fields.interpretation_hints: A reported-availability floor for consumer/small-business fiber, NOT carrier-grade or dark fiber, lit buildings, long-haul routes, or interconnection — a colo site's real fiber question needs a carrier list / a fiber-route map. 0 is a genuine screening red flag (no reported fiber); a higher count is more market activity, not a better interconnect site. BDC over-reports (10-business-day rule). Combine with nearest_urban_area_distance_m. For long-haul/carrier interconnection (NOT mass-market FTTP), see nearest_long_haul_rail_corridor_distance_m + nearest_submarine_cable_distance_m + nearest_gas_pipeline_distance_m.
fields.name: fiber_provider_count
fields.null_meaning: No BDC broadband-serviceable locations in the hex, or the query failed.

fields.description: Whether >=1 ISP reports fiber (FTTP) mass-market availability in the FCC BDC H3 res-8 hexagon containing the point (live ArcGIS Living Atlas mirror).
fields.interpretation_hints: Whether reported consumer FTTP exists at the point (mass-market, reported not installed). False is a real red flag for fiber-dependent uses; True is an availability floor, NOT an interconnect-ecosystem signal — confirm carriers and route diversity directly. Combine with fiber_provider_count. For long-haul/carrier interconnection (NOT mass-market FTTP), see nearest_long_haul_rail_corridor_distance_m + nearest_submarine_cable_distance_m + nearest_gas_pipeline_distance_m.
fields.name: fiber_broadband_available
fields.null_meaning: No BDC broadband-serviceable locations in the hex, or the query failed.

fields.description: Best modeled 5G-NR coverage tier whose polygon contains the point (FCC BDC mobile, max across carriers).
fields.interpretation_hints: Matters for out-of-band management and construction-phase comms at remote greenfield sites. Carrier self-reported (known to overstate).
fields.name: mobile_5g_coverage_class
fields.null_meaning: No modeled 5G-NR coverage at the point, or the FCC BDC mobile fetch failed.

fields.description: Straight-line distance to the nearest 2020 Census Urban Area boundary (0 if inside an urban area).
fields.interpretation_hints: Federally-defensible proxy for nearness to telecom aggregation / fiber meet-me density / lower-latency peering / labor — the public substitute for commercial IXP/metro datasets.
fields.name: nearest_urban_area_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No Census urban area within the search radius.

fields.description: Federal surface-managing agency of the containing parcel (BLM/USFS/NPS/FWS/DOD/BOR/BIA/OTHER_FEDERAL/STATE/PRIVATE_OR_UNKNOWN), from the BLM SMA layer.
fields.interpretation_hints: Determines the permitting regime: BLM/USFS need federal ROW + NEPA, DOD is a non-starter, private follows local zoning. Complements PAD-US manager.
fields.name: surface_management_agency
fields.null_meaning: No SMA polygon at the point or the BLM service fetch failed.

fields.description: FAA Special Use Airspace containing the point (moa / restricted / prohibited / warning / alert / none; most-restrictive when multiple).
fields.interpretation_hints: MOAs/restricted areas are a primary cause of FAA/DOD obstruction objections that kill tall wind turbines/met towers; near-certain DOD Siting Clearinghouse review.
fields.name: special_use_airspace_type
fields.null_meaning: Local FAA SUA asset missing or corrupt (none = no special-use airspace at the point).

fields.description: 2024 Western Solar Plan ROD (Approved Plan) land status of the point on BLM land (available / avoidance / excluded / other / drecp_cdca / western_washington / not_blm_solar_planning_area).
fields.interpretation_hints: From the signed 2024 ROD (Approved Plan). 'available' (~31M ac, 11 western states) is open for a utility-scale solar ROW application; 'excluded' (~131M ac) is off-limits; 'avoidance' is discouraged/avoided (a soft constraint, NOT the same as available); 'drecp_cdca' lies within the CA DRECP/CDCA and is governed by that plan; 'other' is a ROD residual category; 'western_washington' is a WA-specific designation. First-order go/no-go for federal-land solar.
fields.name: blm_solar_application_land_status
fields.null_meaning: Served from a local GeoPackage mirror of the 2024 ROD Approved-Plan layer (data/blm_solar_peis.gpkg, synced from GCS at boot). Off-BLM-land returns not_blm_solar_planning_area, not null; null only when the local asset is missing/corrupt/unsynced on the serving machine.

fields.description: USFWS predicted relative golden-eagle nest-site density (0-1) at the point. Western US only; null elsewhere by design.
fields.interpretation_hints: Golden-eagle take is the single largest avian permitting/litigation risk for western wind; high density signals likely eagle-take-permit, fatality monitoring, curtailment.
fields.name: golden_eagle_nest_density_index
fields.null_meaning: USFWS golden-eagle raster not bootstrapped, or outside the modeled western US.

fields.description: Distance to the nearest existing wind turbine (USGS/LBNL US Wind Turbine Database).
fields.interpretation_hints: Signals a proven-buildable wind regime, interconnection/permitting precedent, and possible repowering adjacency; also flags wake/competition. National incl. offshore.
fields.name: nearest_wind_turbine_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No USWTDB wind turbine within the search radius of the point.

fields.description: Hub height of the nearest USWTDB turbine.
fields.interpretation_hints: Reveals the turbine class developers found economic in this exact wind regime.
fields.name: nearest_wind_turbine_hub_height_m
fields.null_meaning: No USWTDB turbine within radius, or hub height not recorded for the nearest turbine.

fields.description: Total tip height of the nearest USWTDB turbine.
fields.interpretation_hints: Proxy for whether the area permits modern tall (150m+) machines or is FAA/radar/ordinance-constrained to shorter units.
fields.name: nearest_wind_turbine_total_height_m
fields.null_meaning: No USWTDB turbine within radius, or tip height not recorded for the nearest turbine.

fields.description: Nameplate capacity of the project containing the nearest USWTDB turbine.
fields.interpretation_hints: Project scale indicates how much nearby transmission headroom may already be consumed; names the incumbent comparable.
fields.name: nearest_wind_project_capacity_mw
fields.null_meaning: No USWTDB wind turbine within the search radius of the point.

fields.description: Distance to the centroid of the nearest operating utility-scale (>=1MW) ground-mount PV facility (USGS USPVDB; the source carries facility centroids, not footprint polygons).
fields.interpretation_hints: Proxy for resource quality, permittability, and co-location/PPA opportunity; a nearby cluster signals the area already cleared interconnect/land-use/grid hurdles.
fields.name: nearest_utility_solar_facility_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No USPVDB utility-scale solar facility within the search radius of the point.

fields.description: AC nameplate capacity of the nearest utility-scale PV facility (USPVDB).
fields.interpretation_hints: A 300MW neighbor implies far more interconnection headroom and policy acceptance than a single 1MW array.
fields.name: nearest_utility_solar_facility_capacity_mw
fields.null_meaning: No USPVDB utility-scale solar facility within the search radius of the point.

fields.description: Distance to the nearest EPA RE-Powering screened contaminated/disturbed site (brownfield, landfill, mine), from the 2021 RE-Powering Mapper dataset (~190k sites).
fields.interpretation_hints: Siting on/near one can unlock IRA brownfield/energy-community tax adders, faster local acceptance, and avoids greenfield conversion.
fields.name: nearest_repowering_site_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No EPA RE-Powering screened site within the search radius, or the local index is unavailable (bootstrap-pending / corrupt asset).

fields.description: Expansive-soil class (Low / Moderate / High / Very High) of the dominant component, derived from SSURGO linear extensibility (lep_r) via Soil Data Access.
fields.interpretation_hints: Expansive clays cause differential foundation movement and slab cracking — a major cost driver for DC slabs, transformer pads, and ballasted PV/battery foundations. High/Very High flags engineered foundations.
fields.name: soil_shrink_swell_class
fields.null_meaning: Outside the CONUS gNATSGO grid, falls back to live USDA SDA (preserves AK/HI/PR coverage); genuinely unsurveyed (ocean / no live SDA survey) → whole soil block null; or lep_r not populated.

fields.description: SSURGO farmland classification collapsed to an enum (prime / prime_if_conditions_met / statewide_importance / unique / local_importance / not_prime).
fields.interpretation_hints: Prime/statewide-important status triggers Farmland Protection Policy Act review for federally-assisted projects and is the most common local-ordinance basis for blocking utility-scale solar on ag land — a leading community-opposition driver.
fields.name: prime_farmland_classification
fields.null_meaning: Outside the CONUS gNATSGO grid, falls back to live USDA SDA (preserves AK/HI/PR coverage); genuinely unsurveyed (ocean / no live SDA survey) → whole soil block null; or farmland class not populated.

fields.description: Most-recent monthly city-gate natural-gas price for the state (EIA natural-gas/pri/sum, process PG1; latest non-null month).
fields.interpretation_hints: Natural gas is a top data-center siting driver — on-site or nearby gas generation hedges grid-interconnection delay. City-gate is the delivered wholesale price into the local distribution system. State aggregate (areal).
fields.name: natural_gas_citygate_price_usd_per_mcf
fields.null_meaning: Point did not resolve to a U.S. state, or no published city-gate value for the state in the local EIA table (served from a local per-state table; no API key).

fields.description: Most-recent monthly industrial natural-gas price for the state (EIA natural-gas/pri/sum, process PIN; latest non-null month).
fields.interpretation_hints: The price a large industrial gas consumer (e.g. a data-center co-located gas plant) actually pays; cheaper than residential/commercial and the relevant figure for on-site generation economics. State aggregate (areal).
fields.name: natural_gas_industrial_price_usd_per_mcf
fields.null_meaning: Point did not resolve to a U.S. state, or no published industrial value for the state in the local EIA table (served from a local per-state table; no API key).

fields.description: Whether the point falls within a mapped EIA tight-oil / shale-gas play polygon (Lower-48; point-in-polygon).
fields.interpretation_hints: Being inside a shale play is a proxy for cheap, abundant local natural gas — the dominant data-center siting driver for behind-the-meter gas generation. Lower-48 only; AK/HI resolve to False (out of coverage).
fields.name: in_shale_play
fields.null_meaning: The False value is a concrete answer; null (FAILED) only if the local shale-plays asset is missing or corrupt.

fields.description: Name of the primary (largest-area) shale play containing the point; stacked plays are noted in provenance. Absent if not in any play.
fields.interpretation_hints: Identifies the specific resource (e.g. Spraberry, Wolfcamp, Marcellus) so gas-supply economics can be assessed per basin. Plays stack vertically; the largest-area containing play is the primary.
fields.name: nearest_shale_play_name
fields.null_meaning: Point not in any mapped shale play (semantic absence), or FAILED if the local shale-plays asset is missing or corrupt.

fields.description: Name of the USGS sedimentary basin containing the point (point-in-polygon; the clean single-basin "name" label). Absent if not in any mapped basin.
fields.interpretation_hints: A sedimentary basin is the geologic container for oil/gas resources; pairing it with the shale play and gas-price context grounds the natural-gas siting picture. Coverage includes AK and HI.
fields.name: sedimentary_basin_name
fields.null_meaning: Point not in any mapped USGS sedimentary basin (semantic absence), or the local basins asset is unavailable (bootstrap-pending).

fields.description: Geodesic distance to the nearest natural-gas compressor station (HIFLD/EIA point layer; nearest within 200 km).
fields.interpretation_hints: Compressor stations mark major pipeline corridors with deliverable gas volume — proximity is a strong on-site-generation feasibility signal. ~2015 vintage — the only public national compressor dataset (HIFLD portal decommissioned in 2025).
fields.name: nearest_gas_compressor_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No compressor station within 200 km (semantic absence), or the local HIFLD/EIA compressor gpkg was unavailable.

fields.description: Geodesic distance to the nearest underground natural-gas storage facility (HIFLD/EIA point layer; nearest within 200 km).
fields.interpretation_hints: Gas storage buffers seasonal/peak demand and stabilizes supply for a co-located gas plant — proximity reduces fuel-delivery risk. EIA-191 underground storage, as of Dec 2022.
fields.name: nearest_gas_storage_distance_m
fields.null_meaning: No gas storage facility within 200 km (semantic absence), or the local HIFLD/EIA storage gpkg was unavailable.
